summary.text: 女 is an independent picture of a woman, commonly interpreted in early forms as a kneeling or seated figure with hands crossed or engaged in an activity. The accounts differ on the posture and hand detail.

formation.text: Pictographic: the graph represents a woman as a whole figure, not as a combination of separate semantic and phonetic parts. The kneeling or seated posture is a source interpretation; the hand detail varies across descriptions.

components.text: The whole graph depicts a woman; it is not divided here into smaller components. Early descriptions interpret the figure as kneeling or seated, with hands crossed or engaged in an activity.

history.text: Oracle-bone and bronze accounts describe 女 as a kneeling or seated woman. Later bronze forms simplify the seated posture; one account says the original depiction had become difficult to recognize by the Warring States period. This is a reported history of graphic form, not evidence of a change in meaning. The cited individual inscriptions were not dated here, and no ancient inscription image was visually inspected.

The claim that the modern graph is reversed relative to oracle-bone forms, and the reading of a breast in its strokes, are unverified hypotheses in this dossier. Descriptions of the figure’s posture and hands also differ.

uncertainties.text: The evidence supports early female-related use, but no dated individual inscription establishes which sense came first or when the later senses arose. The dossier reports early uses for 母, 毋, 每/悔, 汝 and 如, but does not establish the contexts or dates needed to explain each as borrowing or semantic development.

This account treats 女 as an independent pictograph; the dossier supplies no phonetic component or sound comparison for it. Readings and reconstructions of 女 itself do not establish a component sound relation.

senses.text: Early inscription accounts report female-related uses. The specific examples were not individually dated in this research, so this label marks the earliest documented category in the dossier, not a proven original meaning or priority among early uses. The Han-period Shuowen glosses 女 as ‘woman’.

Early inscription accounts report 女 used for 母, and cited oracle-bone examples include a reading as 母. The evidence describes an early use or overlap, but does not establish its contexts or a semantic development from ‘woman’.

senses.gloss: reported uses for 毋, 每/悔, 汝, 如, and place names
senses.text: Inscription accounts report these uses of the graph. They may involve writing other words with the sign, but the dossier does not establish enough context or sound evidence to explain the mechanism for each one.

A separate lexical reading is recorded for ‘give as a wife’. The supplied historical-reading data distinguishes this word from 女 ‘female’, but gives no dated evidence for when it arose or how it relates semantically to the other sense.
These meanings are listed in modern dictionary or merged definition data. That evidence does not establish their chronology or a path of development from ‘woman’.

limitations.text: Gloss lists and reported early graph uses do not establish dated transitions between the meanings. No semantic-development links are asserted.

overview.text: 女 is a picture of a woman, interpreted in early forms as a kneeling or seated figure. Its shape changed over time; those graphic changes do not by themselves show a change in meaning.

components.text: Read the whole graph as a woman; early descriptions interpret the figure as kneeling or seated.
